prompts.ar-001: Create `contracts/src/tld-staking/protection/CollateralVault.sol` — a UUPS-upgradeable contract (Solidity ^0.8.25, Foundry) where TLD owners lock FLR as a bond against SLD holder rugs. Storage: `mapping(bytes32 tldNamehash => uint256 collateralAmount)`, `mapping(bytes32 => uint256 lockedUntil)`. Key functions: `deposit(bytes32 tldNamehash) external payable` — only callable by TLD owner (verify via existing `IHsrTld.ownerOfNamehash()`), `withdraw(bytes32 tldNamehash, uint256 amount)` — only when `lockedUntil < block.timestamp` and no active slashing holds, `getCollateral(bytes32) view returns (uint256)`, `lockCollateral(bytes32, uint256 duration)` — called by SlashingEngine (ar-004). Add an interface `ICollateralVault.sol` in `contracts/src/tld-staking/interfaces/`. Integrate with BondCurve (ar-002) to enforce minimum collateral based on SLD count. Use ReentrancyGuardUpgradeable and OwnableUpgradeable following the exact pattern in PaymentManagerV2.sol. Write Foundry tests in `contracts/test/foundry/CollateralVault.t.sol` using the ERC1967Proxy pattern from PaymentManagerV2.t.sol. Emit events: `CollateralDeposited`, `CollateralWithdrawn`, `CollateralLocked`, `CollateralSlashed`.
prompts.ar-002: Create `contracts/src/tld-staking/protection/BondCurve.sol` — a stateless library or view-only contract that calculates required collateral amounts. The curve should be: `requiredCollateral = baseBond + (sldCount * perSldBond) + riskMultiplier`. Input parameters: number of active SLDs under the TLD (query from HsrSld via a new view function or pass as param), TLD trust tier (0-4), average SLD price. Key function: `calculateRequired(uint256 sldCount, uint256 avgPriceUsdCents, uint8 trustTier) pure returns (uint256 flrWei)`. Use IFtsoOracle (existing at `contracts/src/tld-staking/interfaces/IFtsoOracle.sol`) for USD-to-FLR conversion if amounts are USD-denominated. Add configurable parameters: `baseBondUsdCents`, `perSldBondUsdCents`, `tierMultipliers[5]` (owner-settable). Create interface `IBondCurve.sol`. Write Foundry tests covering edge cases: zero SLDs, max SLDs, tier transitions. This is consumed by CollateralVault (ar-001) to enforce minimum deposits. Depends on ar-035 (economics model) for parameter values.
prompts.ar-003: Create `contracts/src/tld-staking/protection/RevenueVestingEscrow.sol` — UUPS-upgradeable contract that holds registration/renewal fees in escrow and releases them over a vesting period instead of immediately to the TLD owner. Storage: `struct VestingSchedule { uint256 totalAmount; uint256 released; uint256 startTime; uint256 duration; bytes32 tldNamehash; }`, `mapping(bytes32 tldNamehash => VestingSchedule[]) schedules`. Key functions: `createVesting(bytes32 tldNamehash, address beneficiary, uint256 duration) external payable` — called by PaymentManagerV2 (ar-011), `release(bytes32 tldNamehash, uint256 scheduleIndex)` — releases vested portion using linear vesting formula, `vestedAmount(bytes32, uint256) view returns (uint256)`, `revokeUnvested(bytes32 tldNamehash, uint256 scheduleIndex)` — called by SlashingEngine (ar-004) to claw back unvested funds. Follow the pull-pattern from PaymentManagerV2.sol for withdrawals. Add `pendingWithdrawals` mapping. Write Foundry tests with `vm.warp()` for time-based testing. Depends on ar-036 (vesting schedule design) for duration parameters.
prompts.ar-004: Create `contracts/src/tld-staking/protection/SlashingEngine.sol` — UUPS-upgradeable contract that enforces automated penalties when TLD owners violate health conditions. Storage: `mapping(bytes32 tldNamehash => SlashRecord[])`, `struct SlashRecord { uint256 amount; uint256 timestamp; bytes32 reason; }`. Key functions: `slash(bytes32 tldNamehash, uint256 amount, bytes32 reason) external` — restricted to authorized callers (GracePeriodManager ar-006, DisputeArbitration ar-008), `slashCollateral(bytes32 tldNamehash, uint256 amount)` — calls CollateralVault.lockCollateral() then transfers to InsuranceFund (ar-005) or RefundDistributor (ar-007), `slashVesting(bytes32 tldNamehash)` — calls RevenueVestingEscrow.revokeUnvested(). Implement role-based access: `SLASHER_ROLE` using OpenZeppelin AccessControl or a simple authorized-callers mapping. Emit `Slashed(bytes32 indexed tldNamehash, uint256 amount, bytes32 reason)`. Write Foundry tests simulating slash scenarios. References: ICollateralVault, IRevenueVestingEscrow, IInsuranceFund, IRefundDistributor interfaces.
prompts.ar-005: Create `contracts/src/tld-staking/protection/InsuranceFund.sol` — UUPS-upgradeable contract funded by a percentage of all registration fees plus slashed collateral. Acts as a safety net for SLD holders if individual TLD collateral is insufficient. Storage: `uint256 public totalFundBalance`, `uint256 public feeContributionBps` (e.g., 200 = 2%), `mapping(bytes32 tldNamehash => uint256 claimedFromFund)`. Key functions: `contribute() external payable` — called by PaymentManagerV2 on each registration, `contributeFee(bytes32 tldNamehash) external payable` — auto-deduct from registration flow, `claimForRefund(bytes32 tldNamehash, uint256 amount, address[] sldHolders)` — called by RefundDistributor (ar-007), `getFundBalance() view`. Implement a cap per TLD claim to prevent fund drain. Add owner-configurable `maxClaimPerTldBps` (max % of fund claimable per incident). Follows ReentrancyGuardUpgradeable. Write Foundry tests. Depends on ar-037 (insurance fund mechanics) for fee percentage and cap parameters.
prompts.ar-006: Create `contracts/src/tld-staking/protection/GracePeriodManager.sol` — UUPS-upgradeable contract that manages countdown timers before slashing penalties execute. When a health violation is detected (DNS down, HNS expired, collateral below minimum), a grace period starts. If the TLD owner remediates before expiry, the penalty is cancelled. Storage: `struct GracePeriod { bytes32 tldNamehash; uint8 violationType; uint256 startTime; uint256 duration; bool resolved; bool executed; }`, `mapping(bytes32 => GracePeriod[]) activePeriods`. Key functions: `startGracePeriod(bytes32 tldNamehash, uint8 violationType, uint256 duration) external` — restricted to backend oracle services (ar-013, ar-014, ar-017), `resolveGracePeriod(bytes32 tldNamehash, uint256 periodIndex) external` — marks as resolved, `executeExpiredPeriod(bytes32 tldNamehash, uint256 periodIndex) external` — calls SlashingEngine.slash() if not resolved. ViolationTypes enum: DNS_DOWN=0, HNS_EXPIRED=1, COLLATERAL_LOW=2, ATTESTATION_FAILED=3. Write Foundry tests with vm.warp().
prompts.ar-007: Create `contracts/src/tld-staking/protection/RefundDistributor.sol` — UUPS-upgradeable contract that distributes slashed collateral and insurance fund payouts to affected SLD holders. Storage: `mapping(bytes32 tldNamehash => mapping(address => uint256)) public refundBalances`, `mapping(bytes32 => uint256) public totalRefundPool`. Key functions: `depositRefund(bytes32 tldNamehash) external payable` — called by SlashingEngine (ar-004), `calculateShare(bytes32 tldNamehash, address sldHolder) view returns (uint256)` — pro-rata based on SLD registration price or equal split, `claim(bytes32 tldNamehash) external` — pull-pattern withdrawal for SLD holders, `batchAllocate(bytes32 tldNamehash, address[] holders, uint256[] amounts) external` — called by backend after computing shares. To determine SLD holders, query HsrSld for all tokens with matching parentNamehash. Use Merkle tree distribution for gas efficiency if >50 holders. Write Foundry tests. Follow PaymentManagerV2 pull-pattern.
prompts.ar-008: Create `contracts/src/tld-staking/protection/DisputeArbitration.sol` — UUPS-upgradeable contract for on-chain dispute filing and resolution. Storage: `struct Dispute { bytes32 tldNamehash; address filer; string reason; uint256 filingTime; uint256 bondAmount; DisputeStatus status; address resolver; }`, `enum DisputeStatus { Filed, UnderReview, ResolvedForFiler, ResolvedForTldOwner, Cancelled }`, `mapping(uint256 => Dispute) disputes`, `uint256 disputeCount`. Key functions: `fileDispute(bytes32 tldNamehash, string reason) external payable` — SLD holder stakes a bond, `resolveDispute(uint256 disputeId, bool inFavorOfFiler) external` — restricted to ARBITRATOR_ROLE (platform admin initially, DAO later), `cancelDispute(uint256 disputeId)` — filer can cancel within 24h. If resolved for filer: refund bond + trigger SlashingEngine. If resolved for TLD owner: bond forfeited to TLD owner. Emit events: `DisputeFiled`, `DisputeResolved`, `DisputeCancelled`. Add `minimumBondUsd` configurable by owner. Write Foundry tests covering all resolution paths.
prompts.ar-009: Create `contracts/src/tld-staking/protection/EmergencyPause.sol` — a module contract (not standalone, designed to be inherited or composed) that adds circuit-breaker functionality to the anti-rug protection system. Key functions: `pauseTld(bytes32 tldNamehash) external` — pauses all SLD registrations under a TLD (sets flag readable by SldRegistrationManager), `unpauseTld(bytes32 tldNamehash) external` — only owner/admin, `pauseGlobal() external` — pauses ALL registrations system-wide, `isPaused(bytes32 tldNamehash) view returns (bool)`. Storage: `mapping(bytes32 => bool) tldPaused`, `bool globalPaused`. Restricted to PAUSER_ROLE (owner + SlashingEngine). Integration point: SldRegistrationManager._register() must check `!emergencyPause.isPaused(tldNamehash)` before proceeding. This requires a UUPS upgrade to SldRegistrationManager to add the check. Write Foundry tests. Consider also pausing CollateralVault withdrawals when TLD is paused.
prompts.ar-010: Create `contracts/src/tld-staking/protection/ReAttestationGate.sol` — UUPS-upgradeable contract requiring TLD owners to periodically re-verify Handshake ownership via FDC. Storage: `mapping(bytes32 tldNamehash => uint256 lastAttestationTime)`, `uint256 public attestationInterval` (e.g., 90 days), `mapping(bytes32 => bool) public attestationRequired`. Key functions: `recordAttestation(bytes32 tldNamehash, IWeb2Json.Proof calldata proof) external` — verifies FDC proof (reuse proof verification logic from TldClaimManager.completeStake() at line 197-237 of TldClaimManager.sol), specifically the FDC proof decoding of abiEncodedData and `flr:0x...` address parsing. `isAttestationCurrent(bytes32 tldNamehash) view returns (bool)` — returns `block.timestamp <= lastAttestationTime[tldNamehash] + attestationInterval`. `getAttestationDeadline(bytes32 tldNamehash) view returns (uint256)` — returns lastAttestationTime + attestationInterval. `setAttestationInterval(uint256 newInterval) external onlyOwner`. Import the same FDC contracts from TldClaimManager: `ContractRegistry` from `@flarenetwork/flare-periphery-contracts/coston2/ContractRegistry.sol`, `IFdcVerification`, `IWeb2Json`. Also verify TLD is still in CLOSED state and not expired on Handshake during re-attestation. If attestation lapses, backend service (ar-015) triggers GracePeriodManager.startGracePeriod(). Emit `AttestationRecorded(bytes32 indexed tldNamehash, uint256 timestamp)` and `AttestationLapsed(bytes32 indexed tldNamehash)`. Create interface `IReAttestationGate.sol`. Write Foundry tests in `contracts/test/foundry/ReAttestationGate.t.sol` using mock FDC proofs — reference the MockFdcVerification pattern in `contracts/test/foundry/FdcStaking.t.sol`.
prompts.ar-011: Upgrade PaymentManagerV2 (`contracts/src/tld-staking/orchestration/PaymentManagerV2.sol`) to route a configurable percentage of each payment through the vesting system. Add new storage variables (UUPS-safe, append after existing): `address public vestingEscrow`, `uint256 public vestingBps` (e.g., 7000 = 70% vested), `address public insuranceFund`, `uint256 public insuranceFeeBps` (e.g., 200 = 2%). Modify `processPayment()`: after calculating platformAmount and ownerAmount, split ownerAmount into `vestedPortion = ownerAmount * vestingBps / 10000` and `immediatePortion = ownerAmount - vestedPortion`. Send vestedPortion to RevenueVestingEscrow.createVesting(). Deduct insuranceFeeBps from total and send to InsuranceFund.contribute(). Add setter functions: `setVestingEscrow()`, `setVestingBps()`, `setInsuranceFund()`, `setInsuranceFeeBps()` — all onlyOwner. Write a new deploy script `scripts/upgrade-payment-manager-v3.js` using the UUPS upgrade pattern from existing scripts. Update Foundry tests in `PaymentManagerV2.t.sol`. Depends on ar-003 and ar-005.
prompts.ar-012: Create `contracts/src/tld-staking/protection/TldMigrationEscrow.sol` — UUPS-upgradeable contract enabling safe TLD ownership transfers without rug risk. When a TLD is sold/transferred, SLD holders get protection during the transition. Storage: `struct Migration { bytes32 tldNamehash; address seller; address buyer; uint256 escrowAmount; uint256 initiatedAt; uint256 completionDeadline; MigrationStatus status; }`, `mapping(bytes32 => Migration) migrations`. Key functions: `initiateMigration(bytes32 tldNamehash, address buyer) external payable` — TLD owner locks extra collateral + proposed terms, `acceptMigration(bytes32 tldNamehash) external` — buyer confirms + deposits matching collateral, `completeMigration(bytes32 tldNamehash) external` — after cooldown period, transfers TLD NFT via HsrTld (requires approval), releases funds. `cancelMigration()` — refunds both parties. Add a cooldown period (e.g., 7 days) for SLD holders to be notified. Emit `MigrationInitiated`, `MigrationCompleted`, `MigrationCancelled`. Write Foundry tests.
prompts.ar-013: Create `backend/src/services/dnsHealthMonitor.js` — a service that periodically probes DNS resolution for all active TLDs and their SLDs to detect DNS failures that would indicate a TLD owner rug. Architecture: Poll every 5 minutes via `setInterval`. For each active TLD in `tlds_v2` table, resolve `ns1.<tld>` and a sample SLD using `dig @localhost -p 5300 <domain> A` via child_process exec (same pattern as BindZoneService in `pdns.js`). Also probe the DoH endpoint: `https://dns.halcyon-names.io/resolve?name=<domain>&type=A`. Store results in a new `tld_health_checks` table (create migration in `backend/src/db/migrate.js`): columns `tld_id, check_type, status, response_time_ms, error_message, checked_at`. If a TLD fails 3 consecutive checks, update `tld_health_score` (ar-016) and trigger alert via notification service (ar-020). Export class `DnsHealthMonitor` with `start()`, `stop()`, `checkTld(tldLabel)` methods. Add to backend startup in `backend/src/index.js`.
prompts.ar-014: Create `backend/src/services/hnsRenewalWatcher.js` — a service that monitors Handshake TLD expiry dates to detect when a staked TLD is approaching expiry or has lapsed. Use the existing `hsdClient.js` service (`hsd-cli rpc getnameinfo <name>`) to query each staked TLD's status. Poll every 6 hours. For each TLD in `tlds_v2`, call `hsdClient.getNameInfo(tldLabel)` and check the `info.stats.renewalPeriodEnd` or `info.state` fields. Store results in `tld_hns_status` table: `tld_id, hns_state, hns_expiry_block, hns_renewal_deadline, last_checked_at`. Alert thresholds: WARN at 30 days before expiry, CRITICAL at 14 days, EMERGENCY at 7 days. When CRITICAL, call GracePeriodManager (ar-006) via backend contract interaction. Use ethers.js v6 to call the on-chain contract. Depends on hsdClient.js and hns.js (existing services).
prompts.ar-015: Create `backend/src/services/reAttestationScheduler.js` — a background service that tracks when TLD owners need to re-verify Handshake ownership via FDC. Export class `ReAttestationScheduler` with `start()`, `stop()`, `checkAll()`, `checkTld(tldId)` methods. On startup, query all rows from `tlds_v2` WHERE `lifecycle_state = 'active'`. For each, call ReAttestationGate contract (ar-010) via ethers.js v6: `getAttestationDeadline(tldNamehash)` and `isAttestationCurrent(tldNamehash)`. Use the RPC provider pattern from `stakingListener.js` — import `createFallbackProvider` from `backend/src/utils/rpcProvider.js`. ABI fragment: `const RE_ATTESTATION_ABI = ['function getAttestationDeadline(bytes32) view returns (uint256)', 'function isAttestationCurrent(bytes32) view returns (bool)']`. Poll daily via `setInterval(86400000)`. Store schedule in `tld_attestation_schedule` table (created by ar-041): columns `tld_id INTEGER REFERENCES tlds_v2(id), last_attestation TIMESTAMP, next_deadline TIMESTAMP, reminder_30d_sent BOOLEAN DEFAULT false, reminder_14d_sent BOOLEAN DEFAULT false, reminder_7d_sent BOOLEAN DEFAULT false, grace_started BOOLEAN DEFAULT false`. Send tiered email reminders using existing `emailService.js` (import from `backend/src/services/emailService.js`): 30 days = informational, 14 days = warning, 7 days = urgent. If deadline passes with no re-attestation, use a signer (from `config.operatorPrivateKey`) to call `GracePeriodManager.startGracePeriod(tldNamehash, 3, 604800)` on-chain (violationType 3 = ATTESTATION_FAILED, 7 day grace). Also trigger alertNotificationService (ar-020). Log all actions using `loggers.reAttestation` (add to logger config). Register in `backend/src/index.js` alongside other background services.
prompts.ar-016: Create `backend/src/services/tldHealthScore.js` — an engine that computes a composite health score (0-100) for each TLD. Inputs: DNS health (from ar-013), HNS renewal status (from ar-014), collateral ratio (from CollateralVault ar-001 on-chain query), attestation freshness (from ar-010), dispute history, vesting compliance. Formula: `score = w1*dnsScore + w2*hnsScore + w3*collateralScore + w4*attestationScore + w5*historyScore` where weights are configurable. Store in `tld_health_scores` table: `tld_id, overall_score, dns_score, hns_score, collateral_score, attestation_score, history_score, computed_at`. Expose via API in `routesV2.js`: `GET /api/v2/tld/:label/health` returning the score breakdown. Map score ranges to trust tiers: 90-100=Platinum, 70-89=Gold, 50-69=Silver, 25-49=Bronze, 0-24=At Risk. Cache scores in Redis (existing `cache.js` service) with 15-minute TTL. Recompute on demand or every 15 minutes.
prompts.ar-017: Create `backend/src/services/collateralOracle.js` — a service that reads on-chain collateral state from CollateralVault and BondCurve contracts, syncs to PostgreSQL, and triggers alerts on undercollateralization. Export class `CollateralOracleService` with `start()`, `stop()`, `syncAll()`, `syncTld(tldId)` methods. Use ethers.js v6 with `createFallbackProvider()` from `backend/src/utils/rpcProvider.js`. ABI fragments (human-readable, matching stakingListener.js pattern): `const COLLATERAL_VAULT_ABI = ['function getCollateral(bytes32) view returns (uint256)', 'function lockedUntil(bytes32) view returns (uint256)']` and `const BOND_CURVE_ABI = ['function calculateRequired(uint256, uint256, uint8) view returns (uint256)']`. Poll every 10 minutes via setInterval. For each TLD in `tlds_v2`, read on-chain collateral via `vault.getCollateral(tldNamehash)`, compute required via `bondCurve.calculateRequired(sldCount, avgPriceUsdCents, trustTier)` where sldCount comes from `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM slds_v2 WHERE tld_id = $1 AND expiry_time > NOW()` and avgPrice from `SELECT AVG(registration_price_usd_cents) FROM slds_v2 WHERE tld_id = $1`. Store in `tld_collateral_status` table (ar-041): `tld_id, current_collateral_flr NUMERIC(36,18), required_collateral_flr NUMERIC(36,18), ratio_bps INTEGER, deficit_flr NUMERIC(36,18), is_sufficient BOOLEAN, locked_until TIMESTAMP, last_synced_at TIMESTAMP`. If ratio_bps < 10000 (undercollateralized), call `tldLifecycleStateMachine.transition(tldId, 'WARNING', 'COLLATERAL_LOW')` and trigger GracePeriodManager on-chain. Expose API endpoint in routesV2.js: `GET /api/v2/tld/:label/collateral` returning full status. Cache in Redis with 10-minute TTL.
prompts.ar-018: Create `backend/src/services/slashingProcessor.js` — an event listener service that monitors SlashingEngine (ar-004) and related protection contract events, updating PostgreSQL state in real-time. Export class `SlashingProcessorService` with `start()`, `stop()` methods. Follow the exact architecture of `stakingListener.js` (at `backend/src/services/stakingListener.js`): use `createFallbackProvider()` from `backend/src/utils/rpcProvider.js`, block-polling loop with configurable interval (default 12 seconds to match Flare block time), store last-processed-block in `processed_events` table for idempotent restartable processing. ABI definitions: `const SLASHING_ENGINE_ABI = ['event Slashed(bytes32 indexed tldNamehash, uint256 amount, bytes32 reason)', 'event VestingRevoked(bytes32 indexed tldNamehash, uint256 amount)']`. On Slashed event: 1) Look up tld_id from tlds_v2 by namehash, 2) Insert into `tld_slash_history` table with tx_hash, block_number, ethers.formatEther(amount), 3) Call collateralOracle.syncTld(tldId) to refresh collateral status, 4) Call tldHealthScore.recompute(tldId) to update health score, 5) Query all SLD holders: `SELECT DISTINCT owner_address FROM slds_v2 WHERE tld_id = $1 AND expiry_time > NOW()`, 6) Send alerts to each via alertNotificationService.sendAlert('SLASH_EXECUTED', tldNamehash, holders, {amount, reason}), 7) Check if health score crossed a tier boundary and trigger TRUST_TIER_CHANGE alert if so. Also listen for GracePeriodStarted, GracePeriodResolved, GracePeriodExpired events from GracePeriodManager (ar-006). Can be integrated as additional event handlers within stakingListener.js or run as a standalone PM2 process.
prompts.ar-019: Create `backend/src/services/vestingReleaseProcessor.js` — a service that monitors vesting schedules and processes releases for TLD owner revenue. Export class `VestingReleaseProcessor` with `start()`, `stop()`, `processAll()`, `processSchedule(scheduleId)` methods. Two modes of operation: 1) Event listener mode — listen for `VestingCreated(bytes32 indexed tldNamehash, address beneficiary, uint256 amount, uint256 duration)` and `VestingReleased(bytes32 indexed tldNamehash, uint256 scheduleIndex, uint256 amount)` events from RevenueVestingEscrow (ar-003) using the block-polling pattern from stakingListener.js. On VestingCreated: insert into `vesting_schedules` table. On VestingReleased: update `released_amount` and insert into `vesting_releases` table. 2) Polling mode — every hour via setInterval, query all active schedules: `SELECT * FROM vesting_schedules WHERE released_amount < total_amount`. For each, call `vestingEscrow.vestedAmount(tldNamehash, scheduleIndex)` view function via ethers.js v6. If vestedAmount > released_amount, compute `releasable = vestedAmount - released_amount`. If releasable > 0 and backend has signer authority (OPERATOR_ROLE), auto-call `vestingEscrow.release(tldNamehash, scheduleIndex)`. Otherwise, send notification to beneficiary via alertNotificationService (ar-020) with type VESTING_RELEASE_AVAILABLE. ABI: `const VESTING_ABI = ['function vestedAmount(bytes32,uint256) view returns (uint256)', 'function release(bytes32,uint256)', 'event VestingCreated(bytes32 indexed,address,uint256,uint256)', 'event VestingReleased(bytes32 indexed,uint256,uint256)']`. Store release history in `vesting_releases` table. Expose API in routesV2.js: `GET /api/v2/vesting?owner=<address>` and `GET /api/v2/vesting/:tld/schedules`.
prompts.ar-020: Create `backend/src/services/alertNotificationService.js` — a centralized alert dispatch service for all anti-rug protection events. Export singleton class `AlertNotificationService` with methods: `sendAlert(alertType, tldNamehash, recipients[], data)` — dispatches to all configured channels, `getAlertsForUser(walletAddress, { limit, offset, unreadOnly })` — paginated query, `markRead(alertId, walletAddress)` — marks as read, `getUnreadCount(walletAddress)`. Extend the existing notification infrastructure: import `emailService` from `backend/src/services/emailService.js` for email channel, import `webhookNotificationService` (ar-034) for webhook channel. Alert types enum: `DNS_FAILURE`, `HNS_EXPIRY_WARNING`, `COLLATERAL_LOW`, `SLASH_EXECUTED`, `ATTESTATION_LAPSING`, `DISPUTE_FILED`, `DISPUTE_RESOLVED`, `VESTING_RELEASE_AVAILABLE`, `GRACE_PERIOD_STARTED`, `GRACE_PERIOD_EXPIRED`, `TRUST_TIER_CHANGE`, `MIGRATION_INITIATED`. For each alert, determine recipients based on type: SLASH_EXECUTED/DNS_FAILURE -> all SLD holders under the TLD (query `SELECT DISTINCT owner_address FROM slds_v2 WHERE tld_id = $1 AND expiry_time > NOW()`), COLLATERAL_LOW/ATTESTATION_LAPSING -> TLD owner only, DISPUTE_FILED -> TLD owner + filer. Store in `protection_alerts` table (ar-041): `id SERIAL, alert_type VARCHAR(50), tld_id INTEGER REFERENCES tlds_v2(id), recipient_address CHAR(42), data_json JSONB, sent_via VARCHAR(20)[] DEFAULT '{"in_app"}', read BOOLEAN DEFAULT false, created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW()`. Email templates: use existing emailService pattern with alert-type-specific subject lines and HTML bodies. API endpoints (add to routesV2.js): `GET /api/v2/alerts?wallet=0x...&unread=true&limit=20` — requires wallet auth, `PUT /api/v2/alerts/:id/read` — requires wallet auth + ownership check, `GET /api/v2/alerts/count?wallet=0x...` — unread count for badge display.
prompts.ar-021: Create dispute resolution API endpoints in `backend/src/api/routesV2.js` (append to existing router). Endpoints: `POST /api/v2/disputes/file` — body: `{ tldNamehash, reason, sldTokenId }`, validates SLD ownership via on-chain HsrSld.ownerOf(), returns prepared transaction data for frontend to submit to DisputeArbitration contract (ar-008). `GET /api/v2/disputes?tld=<label>` — lists all disputes for a TLD from `disputes` table. `GET /api/v2/disputes/:id` — single dispute detail with timeline. `PUT /api/v2/disputes/:id/resolve` — admin-only (use existing admin auth middleware from `adminRoutes.js`), submits resolution tx. Create `disputes` table in migrate.js: `id, dispute_id_onchain, tld_id, filer_address, reason, bond_amount_flr, status, resolution, resolver_address, filed_at, resolved_at`. Listen for DisputeFiled/DisputeResolved events in slashingProcessor (ar-018) to keep DB in sync.
prompts.ar-022: Create `backend/src/services/tldLifecycleStateMachine.js` — a state machine that tracks each TLD through its lifecycle stages: PENDING_STAKE -> ACTIVE -> WARNING -> GRACE_PERIOD -> SUSPENDED -> SLASHED -> MIGRATING -> DEREGISTERED. Store state in existing `tlds_v2` table (add column `lifecycle_state VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'active'`). State transitions triggered by: ar-013 (DNS health), ar-014 (HNS renewal), ar-015 (attestation), ar-017 (collateral), ar-018 (slashing), ar-012 (migration). Key functions: `transition(tldId, newState, reason)` — validates transition is legal (define allowed transitions map), logs in `tld_state_transitions` table: `id, tld_id, from_state, to_state, reason, triggered_by, timestamp`. Each transition triggers appropriate actions: WARNING -> send alerts, GRACE_PERIOD -> start timer, SUSPENDED -> pause registrations, SLASHED -> trigger refunds. Export as singleton class. Consumed by all other ar-0XX backend services.
prompts.ar-023: Create two files: `frontend/components/protection/TrustTierBadge.tsx` and `frontend/hooks/useTldHealth.ts`. The badge is a React component that displays the trust tier for a TLD as a colored badge with optional tooltip. newTasks.prompt: Create `contracts/src/tld-staking/protection/SldHolderEnumeration.sol` — a view-only helper contract (no state mutations) that provides efficient enumeration of SLD holders under a TLD. The existing HsrSld contract stores `parentNamehash` per token but has no way to enumerate all tokens by parent. This contract adds that capability. This contract should provide on-chain verification: `isHolderUnderTld(bytes32 tldNamehash, address holder) view returns (bool)` — checks if holder owns any SLD with that parentNamehash by iterating their token balance (expensive for large holders, but useful for small counts). Also add `getActiveSldCount(bytes32 tldNamehash) view returns (uint256)` — stored counter incremented on mint, decremented on burn/expiry. This requires a UUPS upgrade to HsrSld to add `mapping(bytes32 parentNamehash => uint256 activeSldCount)` and update it in mint/burn. Alternatively, make this a backend-only indexed value. Write Foundry tests.

newTasks.prompt: Extend `backend/src/services/stakingListener.js` to listen for events emitted by the anti-rug protection contracts. Add new ABI definitions following the existing pattern (human-readable event strings): COLLATERAL_VAULT_ABI: `CollateralDeposited(bytes32 indexed tldNamehash, uint256 amount)`, `CollateralWithdrawn(...)`, `CollateralSlashed(...)`, `CollateralLocked(...)`. SLASHING_ENGINE_ABI: `Slashed(bytes32 indexed tldNamehash, uint256 amount, bytes32 reason)`. DISPUTE_ABI: `DisputeFiled(uint256 indexed disputeId, bytes32 indexed tldNamehash, address filer)`, `DisputeResolved(...)`. VESTING_ABI: `VestingCreated(...)`, `VestingReleased(...)`. GRACE_PERIOD_ABI: `GracePeriodStarted(...)`, `GracePeriodResolved(...)`, `GracePeriodExpired(...)`. In the constructor, instantiate new contract objects from `config.contractsV2.protectionRegistry`, etc. (add addresses to `backend/src/config/index.js`). Add handler methods following the existing pattern: `handleCollateralDeposited()`, `handleSlashExecuted()`, etc. Each handler: 1) checks `processed_events` table for idempotency, 2) updates relevant DB table, 3) triggers alertNotificationService (ar-020). Load contract addresses from `deployments/coston2-anti-rug.json`.

newTasks.title: Anti-Rug Protection Foundry Test Helpers
newTasks.description: Shared test helper contracts and utilities for all anti-rug protection Foundry tests, including mock contracts for FDC verification, FtsoOracle, and the existing V2 system.
newTasks.prompt: Create `contracts/test/foundry/helpers/AntiRugTestBase.sol` — a shared base test contract that all anti-rug protection tests inherit from. This eliminates setup duplication across 12+ test files. Include: 1) Deploy full V2 system (HsrTld, HsrSld, SldRegistrationManager, PaymentManagerV2, FtsoOracle, etc.) behind UUPS proxies — extract from existing test setUp() patterns in `contracts/test/foundry/`. 2) Deploy all protection contracts (CollateralVault, SlashingEngine, etc.) and wire them together. 3) Helper functions: `_mintTld(string label, address owner)`, `_registerSld(string label, bytes32 tldNamehash, address buyer)`, `_depositCollateral(bytes32 tldNamehash, uint256 amount)`, `_advanceTime(uint256 seconds)` using `vm.warp()`. 4) Mock contracts: `MockFtsoOracle` (already exists in `contracts/test/foundry/helpers/` — check and extend), `MockFdcVerification` (for ReAttestationGate tests). 5) Common test addresses: `owner`, `tldOwner`, `sldHolder1-3`, `arbitrator`, `operator`. Reference `contracts/test/foundry/helpers/` directory for existing helper patterns.
